stories.title: Morehouse, Atrium Health Advancing $700M Hospital Project
stories.excerpt: Morehouse School of Medicine and Atrium Health are moving forward with plans for a new teaching hospital at 675 Metropolitan Parkway SW, which will include a network of primary, urgent and specialty care designed to reach communities across Central and South Fulton County. Atrium Health is committing more than $700 million in capital and clinical investment to the hospital and broader care network. The goal is to bring a Level III trauma center with more care closer to where people live. Plans include an acute care hospital, primary care practices, locations combining primary and urgent care, specialty services, virtual and community-based care and a healthplex offering services such as imaging, infusion, endoscopy and emergency care. The new hospital is planned to open with approximately 50 beds with the ability to expand to over 700 beds over time as community needs grow. It will deliver 24/7 emergency and Level III trauma, obstetrics and a neonatal intensive care unit, adult critical care, advanced imaging, cardiac catheterization, interventional radiology and endoscopy. The post Morehouse, Atrium Health Advancing $700M Hospital Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Morehouse School of Medicine and Atrium Health committing $700M to new teaching hospital at 675 Metropolitan Parkway SW, Atlanta.
Level III trauma center opening with ~50 beds, expandable to 700+ beds; full services across primary, urgent, specialty care.
Serves Central and South Fulton County, underserved region lacking trauma and obstetric/NICU capacity.
stories.summary: Morehouse and Atrium Health are advancing a $700M hospital project in South Fulton County, Atlanta, anchored by a Level III trauma center, primary care network, and specialty services. The acute care facility will open with approximately 50 beds and capacity to expand to over 700 beds as demand grows. The project targets underserved communities across Central and South Fulton County with 24/7 emergency, obstetrics, NICU, and advanced imaging.
stories.impact: Major anchor institutional investment signals confidence in South Fulton population and economic fundamentals, creating a 5–10 year tailwind for residential absorption in the submarket. A 700-bed hospital expansion implies significant healthcare-sector job creation and in-migration of clinical staff and support workers—strong rental demand drivers. Developers should target multifamily sites within 1–2 miles of the campus for workforce housing and service-industry employees.

stories.title: Investor Team Scores $53.5M Refi on Doral Center Offices
stories.excerpt: Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management landed a $53.5 million loan for the refinancing of the Doral Center complex, located at the intersection of Doral Boulevard and NW 87th Avenue in Doral. A CBRE team led by Amy Julian and Andrew Chilgren secured the financing through Wells Fargo. The financing follows a comprehensive $15.5 million capital investment program that transformed the property into a Class A office destination. Major upgrades to the asset include a newly constructed parking structure, full elevator modernization, updated building lobbies, refreshed common areas and facades and high-quality tenant improvements and move-in ready spec suites. “The extensive capital improvements have completely transformed Doral Center into a premier workplace environment,” said CBRE’s Julian. The two-building property was acquired by Banyan and Indepencia in 2021. At the time, it was 30% leased. Today, that number stands at 85%. Banyan is also currently marketing a build-to-suit opportunity of up to 60,000 square feet in the center of the park. The post Investor Team Scores $53.5M Refi on Doral Center Offices appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management refinanced Doral Center offices for $53.5M via Wells Fargo.
Asset improved from 30% to 85% leased after $15.5M capital program; two-building complex now Class A.
Doral, Miami metro, shows office recovery driven by capital and tenant repositioning rather than new demand.
stories.summary: Banyan Street Capital and Independencia Asset Management secured a $53.5M refinance for the Doral Center office complex in Doral, Florida, following a $15.5M capital investment that transformed the two-building property into a Class A asset. Occupancy surged from 30% to 85% post-renovation. The lenders are marketing a 60,000-square-foot build-to-suit opportunity within the center.
stories.impact: Doral office market stabilizing via value-add recapitalization, not organic demand growth. For multifamily developers, this signals cautious office-market recovery; however, Doral's affordability relative to Miami proper may sustain residential demand from service-sector and administrative workers. Build-to-suit appetite suggests some employment growth—monitor further corporate leasing activity before committing land to residential in Doral proper.

stories.title: BTH Breaks Ground on 7-Building Port St. Lucie Warehouse Development
stories.excerpt: BTH Development Partners is moving ahead on Phase 1 of Tradition Commerce Park, a 530,000 square foot industrial park in Port St. Lucie. Miller Construction Company is building the project at 12051 SW Tom Mackie Boulevard. Claren Architecture and Planners is the architect., Tradition Commerce Park is master-planned industrial and flex development spanning about 34 acres. Developed by BTH Development Partners, Tradition Commerce Park is approved for seven industrial and flex buildings. Phase 1 encompasses vertical construction of Building 4 (approximately 28,800 square feet) and Building 5 (approximately 26,400 square feet). Both Phase 1 buildings features customizable tenant layouts, starting at 3,000 square feet, to meet the region’s surging demand for small- to mid-bay flex and light industrial space. Subsequent phases of Tradition Commerce Park are planned to deliver large-bay dock-high industrial distribution facilities of up to 166,968 square feet, as well as build-to-suit opportunities. Colliers International Florida serves as the exclusive leasing and sales brokerage for the development. The post BTH Breaks Ground on 7-Building Port St. Lucie Warehouse Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BTH Development Partners breaking ground on Phase 1 of Tradition Commerce Park, Port St. Lucie, Florida: 530,000 SF master plan.
Phase 1: Buildings 4 and 5 (55,200 SF combined), flex/light industrial with 3,000 SF minimum lease blocks.
Seven-building, 34-acre industrial park approved; subsequent phases include large-bay dock-high and build-to-suit distribution.
stories.summary: BTH Development Partners is beginning vertical construction on Phase 1 of Tradition Commerce Park, a 530,000-square-foot industrial park in Port St. Lucie, Florida. Phase 1 delivers two flex buildings (Buildings 4 and 5) totaling 55,200 square feet with customizable small-to-mid-bay layouts starting at 3,000 square feet. Subsequent phases will include large-bay dock-high industrial distribution facilities up to 166,968 square feet.
stories.impact: Port St. Lucie industrial supply growth targeting small/mid-bay flex demand. For multifamily developers, this indicates supply-chain/logistics job creation and workforce-housing opportunity in Port St. Lucie. However, the absorption timeline and tenant mix (flex vs. distribution) should be tracked; if flex space absorbs slowly, it may signal softer local employment than headlines suggest. Monitor job growth announcements in the port and logistics sectors for residential demand validation.

stories.title: Circle Realty Secures 38K SF of New Leases at 14 Penn Plaza
stories.excerpt: Circle Realty Group has closed on 37,600 square feet of new leases in Midtown, Commercial Observer has learned. The two largest deals at 225 West 34th Street, also known as 14 Penn Plaza, were for civil engineering company Bohler Engineering, which expanded from 8,000 square feet to 14,000 square feet, and cybersecurity firm T&M USA, which took 14,000 square feet, according to Circle Realty. Bohler signed a 10-year lease and asking rent in the building was $67 per square foot. The length of T&M’s lease was unclear. “These tenants came to me because we’re at the center of transportation and we have a first-class property,” Circle Realty President Jay Futersak told CO. “Tenants know that what we promised is what we deliver.” Futersak represented his own firm in-house and both tenants in the deals. Smaller recent deals in the building were for accounting and advisory firm Calibre CPA Group, which signed a 10-year, 6,100-square-foot lease and is relocating from 462 Seventh Avenue. Mark Furst and Benjamin Saftler of Kaufman Leasing, the brokerage arm of the Kaufman Organization, handled the deal for the Washington, D.C.-based accounting firm and did not immediately comment. Meanwhile, discrimination law firm Fitapelli & Schaffer is also relocating from 20 Liberty Street to 14 Penn with a new 3,514-square-foot lease. Robert Gallucci of Colliers negotiated on behalf of the law firm and did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Futersak repped ownership in-house in the Calibre and Fitapelli deals. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Circle Realty Group closed 37,600 SF of new office leases at 14 Penn Plaza (225 West 34th Street), Midtown Manhattan.
Bohler Engineering expanded 8,000 to 14,000 SF (10-year, $67/SF); T&M USA took 14,000 SF; Calibre CPA Group 6,100 SF.
Professional and tech tenants clustering in Midtown near Penn Station on long-term leases; stable, not speculative demand.
stories.summary: Circle Realty Group closed 37,600 square feet of new office leases at 14 Penn Plaza in Midtown Manhattan, including expansions by civil engineering firm Bohler Engineering (to 14,000 SF, 10-year term at $67/SF) and cybersecurity firm T&M USA (14,000 SF). Smaller deals included accounting firm Calibre CPA Group at 6,100 SF. Leases reflect professional services and tech tenant demand for well-maintained, transit-accessible space.
stories.impact: Modest but steady office absorption in Midtown Manhattan tied to professional services, engineering, and cybersecurity clusters. For multifamily developers, this confirms continued white-collar employment and high-wage tenant migration to Manhattan, supporting luxury rental demand near Penn Station and Midtown. Long-term lease commitments (10 years) signal employer confidence; however, the transaction size is incremental, not transformative—expect slow, steady rental growth rather than sharp spikes in Midtown residential.

stories.title: Sunday Summary: Who’s Funding $1.3 Trillion in Data Center Spending?
stories.excerpt: Pluck your average Commercial Observer journalist off the street, shove them in a van, shine a flashlight in their eyes, and say, “Quick — what’s the biggest story in commercial real estate?” nine reporters out of 10 will answer: “Data centers.” At least that’s the case in 2026 after the billions and billions of dollars in investment that have been lavished on the sector. Actually, make that trillion — with a “t.” It’s still a sector that’s largely mysterious and unknown (even the vocabulary of the asset class is new!) so CO was excited last week when San Diego-based Atrium, an AI analytics firm, launched an interactive data platform called “Who Finances America’s Data Centers,” which tracks the money behind the $1.3 trillion (and counting) data center bonanza. What makes Atrium’s platform so fascinating is that it delves into the nitty gritty of individual deals like Coreweave’s $23 billion debt facility from 38 different lenders, and the 24 lenders financing DigitalBridge and IFM’s $20 billion debt facility — but at the same time it examines the breadth of activity of non-bank lenders like PIMCO (which has done $23 billion in originations), or borrowers like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta and Oracle (five firms that alone account for $223 billion in long-term debt and credit facilities). All this data center activity comes as construction costs have been on the rise. bullets: $1.3 trillion in U.S. data center investment tracked; Coreweave secured $23B debt facility from 38 lenders.
DigitalBridge and IFM raised $20B debt from 24 lenders; PIMCO has $23B in data center originations.
Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle driving hyperscale capex; non-bank lenders (PIMCO, insurance, PE) dominating financing.
stories.summary: Data center investment in the U.S. has reached $1.3 trillion, with major facilities funded through large, multi-lender debt facilities. Coreweave's $23 billion facility involved 38 lenders; DigitalBridge and IFM's $20 billion included 24 lenders. Non-bank lenders like PIMCO have originated $23 billion in data center debt. Tech giants (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle) are the primary drivers of hyperscale capacity expansion.
stories.impact: Data center boom is reshaping real estate capital flows and pricing dynamics. For multifamily developers, this signals: (1) tech-sector jobs and talent concentration in data center hubs (Northern Virginia, Phoenix, Dallas, Denver, California); (2) land scarcity and rising acquisition costs in those markets; (3) indirect residential demand from data center construction workers and IT operational staff. Developers should map data center pipelines and pre-position land in secondary submarkets near hyperscale facilities for workforce housing, as primary sites will remain expensive and constrained.

stories.title: Zimmet Law Group Signs 10-Year Lease for 515 Madison Ave.
stories.excerpt: GFP Real Estate announced that Zimmet Law Group P.C. has signed a new office lease for 5,476 square feet at 515 Madison Ave. in Manhattan’s Plaza District. Zimmet Law Group will occupy Suite 603 on the sixth floor of the building under a new 10-year lease, relocating its Manhattan office from 477 Madison Ave. The firm is expected to take occupancy following completion of its new space later this year. Martin McGrath and Kephra Stone of GFP Real Estate represented the landlord in-house. Elliot Zelinger of Savitt Partners represented Zimmet Law Group. “Zimmet Law Group’s decision to make a long-term commitment to 515 Madison Avenue speaks to the continued appeal of the building and the strength of the Plaza District,” said McGrath. “Professional services firms continue to prioritize high-quality, well-located office space, and we’re pleased to welcome Zimmet Law Group to the building.” The post Zimmet Law Group Signs 10-Year Lease for 515 Madison Ave. appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Zimmet Law Group signed 10-year office lease for 5,476 SF at 515 Madison Ave., Suite 603, Manhattan Plaza District.
Zimmet relocating from 477 Madison Ave.; occupancy expected later in 2026.
Professional services firm commitment to Plaza District reflects sustained appeal of high-quality, trophy Manhattan office assets.
stories.summary: Zimmet Law Group P.C. signed a new 10-year office lease for 5,476 square feet at 515 Madison Avenue in Manhattan's Plaza District, relocating from 477 Madison Avenue. The firm will occupy Suite 603 on the sixth floor, with occupancy expected later in 2026.
stories.impact: Another incremental professional services lease in Plaza District/Midtown Manhattan; consistent with steady, long-term office tenant commitments but not indicative of outsized demand. For multifamily developers, this reinforces Midtown's role as a legal and professional services hub, supporting high-wage rental demand in proximate residential buildings. No market-moving signal on its own.

stories.title: Avison Young Recapitalization Provides “War Chest” for Further Growth

Rose told Connect CRE. “This gives us the war chest to do the things that we’re known for”–namely, make strategic acquisitions, broaden the platform’s capabilities and expand the pool of talent through recruitment. “And we have our eyes on targets.” Expected to close in October, the new transaction builds upon the success of the company’s 2024 recapitalization. It also represents a rethinking of how to produce the best outcome for Avison Young’s longtime financial stakeholders as well as the company’s principals.   “It’s kind of simple,” said Rose. “Was it better to take the money and pay these [stakeholders], or was it better to invest and make them multiples of the same money? And after 16 months, that’s what we were able to come to.”  The process of devising this solution began in the spring of 2025, Rose said. bullets: Avison Young recapitalization reduces debt-to-EBITDA to under 3x, cuts preferred equity and debt by ~70%.
Closing expected October 2026; transaction gives company 'war chest' for strategic acquisitions and platform expansion.
Second recapitalization in 16 months; CEO Mark Rose signals aggressive growth strategy and talent recruitment.
stories.summary: Avison Young announced a recapitalization that deleverage its balance sheet (debt-to-EBITDA below 3x), reduces debt and preferred equity by nearly 70%, and provides common equity positions to key financial partners. The deal is expected to close in October 2026 and follows a 2024 recapitalization. CEO Mark Rose emphasized the capital will fund strategic acquisitions, platform capability expansion, and talent acquisition.
stories.impact: Avison Young's strengthened balance sheet and aggressive acquisition posture signal consolidation activity in CRE services and brokerage. For multifamily developers, this means Avison Young will be a more active competitor in site advisory, market analysis, and brokerage—potentially raising broker commissions and service costs. Monitor M&A activity among mid-market brokerage platforms; consolidation often precedes repricing of advisory services and tighter capital availability for smaller, independent brokers.

stories.title: CoStar Closes $800M Cash Acquisition of New-Home Platform Zonda
stories.excerpt: CoStar Group, a leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information, analytics and 3D digital twin technology, announced that it has completed its acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software and residential real estate marketplace platform, for $800 million in cash. Zonda’s platform of proprietary lot-level construction and development data, which serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders and suppliers, gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market, according to the CoStar announcement. Based in Washington, D.C., Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. CoStar’s acquisition of the platform was first announced in May. “Zonda has built an exceptional business around information the homebuilding industry relies on every day,” Andy Florance, founder and CEO of CoStar, said in announcing the deal’s closing. “This is a massive market with a sophisticated group of builders, developers, lenders, investors and suppliers that need purpose-built information, analytics and marketing solutions. With the acquisition now complete, we have the opportunity to bring together Zonda’s proprietary new construction data, software and builder relationships with CoStar Group’s technology, analytics and marketplace capabilities.” The deal provides Arlington, Va.-based CoStar with new-home data and analytics from Zonda, which tracks new-home communities, land development, construction activity, home sales and builder operations at the lot level. In addition, Zonda-owned residential marketplaces NewHomeSource.com and Livabl join CoStar’s portfolio, expanding its consumer marketplace business specifically into new construction. bullets: CoStar Group completed $800M cash acquisition of Zonda, new-home construction data and software platform.
Zonda generated ~$170M revenue in 2025; serves 3,000+ homebuilders, developers, lenders, suppliers.
$400B annual U.S. new-home sales market; Zonda's lot-level development data and builder software expand CoStar into residential construction pipeline.
stories.summary: CoStar Group completed its $800 million cash acquisition of Zonda, a new-home-construction data, homebuilder software, and residential real estate marketplace platform. Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025 and serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders, and suppliers. The acquisition gives CoStar access to proprietary lot-level construction and development data and a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home market.
stories.impact: CoStar's acquisition of Zonda signals data consolidation in residential real estate and construction—strengthening CoStar's end-to-end intelligence on single-family and multifamily pipelines. For multifamily developers, this means CoStar will have more granular visibility into competitive lot-level supply, builder capacity, and construction-cost trends. Expect upward pressure on CoStar subscription pricing and potential integration of Zonda's homebuilder software into multifamily development workflows. Developers should anticipate tighter competitive intelligence and faster market-cycle awareness among peers using CoStar's expanded platform.

stories.title: Michael Troyanovsky of Regency Development Group: 5 Questions

Regency has four active projects on the island, including the 33-unit La Maré Regency, the nine-unit La Maré Signature and the 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas. Commercial Observer recently caught up with Michael Troyanovsky, managing partner and vice president of the family company, to discuss the submarket’s success. The following conversation has been edited for length and clarity.   Commercial Observer: Why Bay Harbor Islands? What caught your interest about that submarket? We came to the area, and we really felt like it had the most potential. It was always overlooked. It’s honestly the most amazing hidden gem. It’s surrounded by the most beautiful waters, a little nook in the center of Miami. It’s getting more and more discovered. Since then, we really integrated into the island, and we really got to know the local community, the local governments, because we have to work very closely with them on getting all the projects approved and making sure that it fits the neighborhood and demographic. bullets: Regency Development Group has built four active multifamily projects in Bay Harbor Islands, Florida since 2020.
Portfolio includes La Maré Regency (33 units), La Maré Signature (9 units), Bay Harbor Villas (20 units); ~62 units delivered/under construction.
Bay Harbor Islands (pop. <6,000), near Surfside and Bal Harbour, positioned as overlooked luxury coastal submarket.
stories.summary: Regency Development Group has been developing residential projects in Bay Harbor Islands, Florida, a coastal community of fewer than 6,000 residents near Surfside and Bal Harbour, since 2020. The developer currently has four active projects, including La Maré Regency (33 units), La Maré Signature (9 units), and Bay Harbor Villas (20 units). Managing partner Michael Troyanovsky emphasized the submarket's undervaluation relative to comparable nearby communities.
stories.impact: Regency's concentrated build-out in micro-submarket (Bay Harbor Islands) signals discovery of secondary-location luxury demand near Bal Harbour and Surfside. For multifamily developers, this indicates: (1) spillover demand from sold-out Bal Harbour and Surfside to adjacent, lower-profile towns; (2) pricing opportunity in mini-markets with strong location (waterfront access, proximity to luxury retail/dining); (3) potential saturation risk if multiple developers flood the same submarket. Monitor absorption and pricing for the four Regency projects to gauge whether demand is durable or driven by a single operator's scale.

stories.title: JBL Asset Management Buys Retail Condo Near Miami Design District
stories.excerpt: Alta Developers sold off a retail condo near the Miami Design District for $17.3 million, property records show. JBL Asset Management purchased the 25,504-square-foot asset on the ground floor of the Quadro condo building. The property at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard faces train tracks, just east of the Miami Design District, an open-air, luxury mall. Quadro’s retail tenants include The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture store and Waterworks plumbing supply store. Hollywood, Fla.-based JBL is marketing a 2,358-square-foot suite as the last remaining retail space at the 407,498-square-foot condo building. Alta Developers completed the 200-unit building in 2019. The purchase comes as the 18-block Design District, one of the country’s highest-grossing upscale malls, is undergoing a major expansion. Earlier this week, its owners, entities tied to Miami-based Craig Robins and LVMH billionaire Bernard Arnault, scored a $125 million construction loan to build a Snøhetta-designed, mixed-use building. The joint venture also launched sales for Fouquet’s condo and hotel development, designed by Pritzker Prize winner David Chipperfield. Representatives for Alta Developers and JBL Asset Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: JBL Asset Management acquired 25,504 SF retail condo at Quadro building, 3900 Biscayne Blvd., Miami Design District area.
Purchase price $17.3M; Quadro tenants include The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture, Waterworks plumbing supply.
Miami Design District ownership (Craig Robins, LVMH/Bernard Arnault) secured $125M construction loan for new mixed-use expansion; Fouquet's condo/hotel sales launched.
stories.summary: JBL Asset Management purchased a 25,504-square-foot retail condo on the ground floor of the Quadro building at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard near the Miami Design District for $17.3 million. The property faces train tracks east of the Design District and currently houses tenants including The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture, and Waterworks plumbing. JBL is marketing the last remaining 2,358-square-foot retail suite at the 407,498-square-foot condo.
stories.impact: Miami Design District ownership's $125M construction loan for new mixed-use development and Fouquet's luxury condo/hotel launch signal major expansion and capital investment in the district. JBL's retail acquisition near the Design District (not within it) is a secondary play on spillover demand. For multifamily developers, this indicates: (1) luxury residential demand in and around the Design District; (2) ongoing capital influx from LVMH/Robins partnership into Miami; (3) opportunity to develop multifamily workforce housing on Biscayne Boulevard corridor to serve Design District retail, hospitality, and construction workers. Monitor Fouquet's presale momentum and design district foot traffic to gauge residential absorption velocity.
